create.name: Hugh Byrne
create.bio:
Hugh Byrne came to meditation after more than two decades working on human rights and development policy in Latin America and Africa. Buddhist practice changed how he saw that work: he came to feel that the way we pursue justice matters as much as the goal. He has taught mindfulness since 2000, completed the four-year teacher training led by Jack Kornfield and Joseph Goldstein, and is one of the senior teachers at the Insight Meditation Community of Washington (IMCW). He holds a doctorate and lives in Silver Spring, Maryland.

His teaching joins the classic insight practices of mindfulness, loving-kindness and equanimity with everyday life and with care for the wider world. A particular thread is habit change: his two books, The Here-and-Now Habit (2016) and Habit Swap (2020), draw on Buddhist psychology and neuroscience to show how attention can loosen automatic patterns. He often uses poetry and humour in his talks. He leads a weekly online dharma class offered on a donation basis, gives one-to-one meditation guidance, and co-leads residential retreats with Rebecca Hines in the Washington area and abroad. His Insight Timer courses cover the Four Noble Truths and meditation with poetry.

books.title: The Here-and-Now Habit: How Mindfulness Can Help You Break Unhealthy Habits Once and for All
books.author: Hugh G. Byrne
books.description: Combines Buddhist teaching on clinging with findings on how habits form in the brain, then offers short mindfulness exercises for noticing and changing automatic behaviour. It comes with guided audio practices; the foreword is by Tara Brach.

books.title: Habit Swap: Trade In Your Unhealthy Habits for Mindful Ones
books.author: Hugh G. Byrne
books.description: A follow-up to his first book that goes further into practical skills for letting go of unhelpful routines and building kinder ones. Each chapter pairs a short explanation with exercises to try in daily life.

courses.title: Cultivating Peace and Presence in the Sanctuary of Southern Spain
courses.description: A week-long retreat near Málaga, co-led with Rebecca Hines. The first days are given to silent practice of loving-kindness, compassion and equanimity; the rest of the week mixes practice with time to explore the Costa del Sol.

courses.title: Individual Meditation Sessions
courses.description: One-to-one meetings to start or deepen a meditation practice, bring mindfulness into relationships and work, work with habits, or study Buddhist teachings. Appointments are booked through his online scheduler.

courses.title: Keys To The Buddha's Central Teachings
courses.description: A six-day Insight Timer course on the Four Noble Truths, from recognising suffering and its roots in craving to the freedom of letting go and the Eightfold Path. Every day pairs a talk with a guided meditation.
courses.price: Included in Member Plus ($59.99 USD a year)

courses.title: Deepen Your Meditation Practice With Poetry
courses.description: A ten-day Insight Timer course that uses well-loved poems as a doorway into present-moment awareness. Each session reads and reflects on a poem before a guided sit.
courses.price: Included in Member Plus ($59.99 USD a year)

free_resources.title: Hugh Byrne on Insight Timer
free_resources.description: Guided meditations and dharma talks on mindfulness, loving-kindness, self-compassion and working with habits, often woven with poetry. Free to listen to in the app or online.

free_resources.title: Weekly Meditation and Dharma Class
free_resources.description: A Sunday-morning class on Zoom with sitting practice and a talk on Buddhist teachings. It is open to all and offered on a donation (dana) basis.
